hypotheses: The success parameter p is a nonnegative real number.
N is an arbitrary natural number.
conclusions: Mapping the product Bernoulli PMF on functions Fin N → Bool by the number of true coordinates yields the same Nat-valued PMF as mapping PMF.binomial p hp N from Fin (N+1) to Nat by Fin.val.
mathematical_definitions: For f : Fin N → Bool, the success-count statistic is the cardinality of {i : Fin N | f i = true}.
The weight of f is the product over i : Fin N of p when f i = true and 1-p when f i = false.
The Boolean-function PMF is the normalized finite PMF determined by those product weights.
The Nat-valued binomial PMF is the pushforward of PMF.binomial p hp N along Fin.val.
translation.proposition_plain_english: The number of successes among N independent Bernoulli trials with success probability p has the binomial distribution with parameters N and p.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The parameter is represented by NNReal and explicitly satisfies p ≤ 1, so it lies in the probability interval [0,1].
N is arbitrary and may equal zero.
The conclusion is an exact equality of Nat-valued probability mass functions.
The standard binomial PMF is initially supported on Fin (N+1) and must be mapped to Nat for comparison.
There is no apparent vacuity risk: NNReal parameters satisfying p ≤ 1 exist, and the claim includes the boundary cases p = 0, p = 1, and N = 0.
